items.q: Why has the Great Clock stopped?
choices: Its seven gears are out of line
misconceptions: named a broken part the story never mentions
blamed forgetting, but the Jumble moved the gears
mixed up the clock with a locked door
items.why: The clock runs on seven gears, one in each tower. The Jumble knocked them out of line, so the clock stands still until every gear turns again.

items.q: A mix uses 2 cups of oats for every 3 cups of milk. Which amounts make the same mix?
choices: 3 cups of oats, 4 cups of milk
4 cups of oats, 5 cups of milk
4 cups of oats, 6 cups of milk
3 cups of oats, 2 cups of milk
misconceptions: added 1 to each amount instead of scaling
added 2 to each amount instead of doubling
items.why: The same mix means both amounts are multiplied by the same number. 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 2 = 6, so 4 cups of oats go with 6 cups of milk.

items.q: A sample is at −5°C. It warms by 8°. What is its temperature now?
misconceptions: ignored the negative sign and added 5 and 8
moved down the line instead of up
found the right distance from zero but kept the negative sign
items.why: Warming moves up the number line. From −5 it takes 5 steps to reach 0, and 3 more steps make 8, so the sample is at 3°C.
